newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares lose 2.44 pct, rebound off lows.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares lose 2.44 pct, rebound off lows.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted sharp losses on Monday due to early selling prompted by the S&P's expected downgrading of Turkey's long-term foreign currency rating despite a recovery in thin afternoon trade, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed down 2,179.9 points, or 2.44 percent at 87,156.96, after rebounding on reaction buys from an opening low of 84,446 which was down 5.5 percent from Friday.
It had lost 5.37 percent last week amid rumours that the S&P might downgrade Turkey's credit rating and the cancellation of a law allowing the sale of state property by the government.
Trade volume plunged to 10.58 trillion lira ($100.5 million) from Friday's 14.47 trillon ($138.7 million).

"The markets were ready for the S&P's downgrading, it was not a surprise. Nevertheless, the stock market usually shows such agressive reactions, but currency and bond markets were little moved," said Barbaros Alten from Global securities.
"We expect sideways trade in coming days and no major fluctuations are seen in the currency market as well," he said.
Brokers said the market would in coming days await the results of a constitutional court debate on a challenge to a law concerning the privatisation of Turk Telekom.
